title: TrustFlow: Verifiable Agent Workflows
summary: TrustFlow makes agent proposals inspectable through deterministic policy, hash-bound approvals, stable payment identities and independent ledger verification. Built with Meta Muse Code; powered through a typed Meta Responses API boundary. The demo shows accepted fake-mode crash recovery. One real Spark read-only planning request is verified; full live acceptance and Wonder remain pending. Synthetic funds only.
full_description:
An agent can claim a payment succeeded without establishing whether the exact action was authorized or whether a timeout hid a late commit. Blindly retrying can create a second payment.

TrustFlow explores this problem with synthetic accounts and funds. A Planner proposes typed steps; deterministic PolicyEngine classifies risk. High-risk actions require a single-use human decision bound to the plan version and SHA-256 hash. Approval freezes the exact snapshot and authorizes its payment intents.

The Executor checks authorized payloads and stable operation identities at the mutation boundary. SQLite atomically checks an idempotency key, updates balances and records the transaction. Verification reads ledger rows independently, checks approved payloads, intent coverage and conservation. A semantic PASS cannot override deterministic failure. Recovery after uncertain execution retries verification without issuing another transfer.

The developer credits Meta Muse Code as an extensive AI-assisted engineering collaborator; Codex also contributed implementation and independent reviews. The human developer retained final decisions. MetaResponsesProvider integrates structured planning and semantic review through Meta's Responses API, with configurable Muse Spark and Muse Wonder. One real muse-spark-1.3 read-only planning diagnostic completed successfully: 191 input and 974 output tokens, estimated $0.00437825, zero tool executions. Full multi-scenario live acceptance and Wonder inference remain pending.

The 120-second video is a narrated montage of actual accepted M5.2 Chromium screenshots, with labelled editorial crops and captions. It demonstrates exact-hash approval, rejection, late commits, missing evidence and controlled post-COMMIT SIGKILL recovery using FakeLLMProvider. The archived 33-case M4 evaluation is an offline regression gate, not a model benchmark.

After prerequisite installation, reproduce six scenarios with python scripts/run_m52_demo.py --out artifacts/m5.2/latest. New candidates require their own validation. This is a trusted local single-instance SQLite prototype with a shared demo token, no production banking or multi-host exactly-once guarantee. Keep it local; older frontend dependencies have known security advisories.
technology_stack: Windows SAPI for local English narration
meta_model_usage: Meta Muse Code collaboration is attributed by the developer. MetaResponsesProvider uses POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses with strict typed schemas. Spark is the cost-conscious configurable planning/inference option; Wonder is configurable for planning/review. One real Spark read-only plan succeeded at M5.3 c48c2af; no tools executed. Full live acceptance and Wonder inference: PENDING. Video: fake-mode M5.2.
architecture: Next.js UI / FastAPI -> Planner -> deterministic PolicyEngine -> Human Approval when required -> Executor -> SQLite Ledger -> independent Verifier. A semantic reviewer uses the provider boundary after deterministic checks. Recovery reconciles existing operations and retries verification only. Audit payload hashes, workflow-scoped usage, evidence spans and manifests provide observability.
technical_novelty: The prototype connects an exact approved snapshot, backend-owned payment identity and independently read ledger evidence across timeout and post-COMMIT crash boundaries. Re-planning or recovery cannot silently turn a new step into permission for another transfer. This is an engineering design demonstrated in a controlled sandbox, not a new cryptographic primitive or universal distributed exactly-once guarantee.
reproducibility: Historical accepted M5.2: 38cc3942dbd715681d59bfd893e47643210294a9. Integrated M5.3: c48c2affd3dda652e00aca9f690404c82182b694; M5.4: b0558e8da93b3b5ce94d722d0de3fca8348ce1e4. Each new SHA needs its own gates. Canonical fake replay: python scripts/run_m52_demo.py --out artifacts/m5.2/latest. Video remains archived fake-mode evidence.
setup_instructions: Install Python 3.12+, Git, a running Linux-container Docker Engine and Compose 2.24.4+ with !override support. Create/activate a virtual environment, run python -m pip install -e ".[dev,demo]", then python -m playwright install chromium. From the repository root run python scripts/run_m52_demo.py --out artifacts/m5.2/latest. See README for platform notes, short Windows output paths and cleanup behavior. No model key is needed for fake mode.
limitations: Synthetic funds/tools; trusted local single instance, SQLite and shared demo token; no production RBAC, banking integration, public deployment, universal crash/race or multi-host exactly-once guarantee. Full live matrix, Wonder and organizer authenticated form/rules remain pending. M5.3 historical acceptance includes approved exception M53-E1-EXCEPTION-01; not unconditional PASS.
